summary: The default JWT ClaimMapper only supports top-level JWT claim names (via permissionsClaimName config), but cannot read nested claims like ext.permissions. This blocks users of Ory Hydra-based OIDC providers (JumpCloud, etc.) where custom claims are placed under an ext object.
userImpact: Users of Ory Hydra-based OIDC providers (JumpCloud, etc.) cannot authenticate with Temporal because their permission claims are nested in an ext object that the ClaimMapper cannot access.
rootCause: The default JWT ClaimMapper implementation only performs flat key lookups in the JWT claims map and does not support traversing nested/dotted paths.
proposedFix: Modify common/authorization/default_jwt_claim_mapper.go to support dotted path traversal (e.g., ext.permissions) when extracting claim values, with fallback to flat key lookup for backward compatibility.
keyQuote: The default JWT ClaimMapper cannot read claims that are nested inside an object (such as `ext.permissions`). It only supports top-level claim names.
